issues.description: ALTER TABLE no longer accepts multiple comma-separated clauses, regressing previously valid SQL.
issues.detail: The old grammar wrapped the OneOf in Delimited(...), permitting statements like `ALTER TABLE t ADD col_b ..., DROP COLUMN col_a`. The new grammar replaces Delimited with a bare OneOf, so only a single clause per ALTER TABLE is parseable. The deleted fixture line in alter_table.sql confirms this was previously supported. This is a real parser regression for valid T-SQL.

issues.description: IdentityGrammar permits whitespace between sign and digits, accepting `IDENTITY(- 5, 1)`.
issues.detail: Using SignedSegmentGrammar as a separate optional segment before NumericLiteralSegment lets the lexer treat the minus and number as independent tokens. T-SQL requires the seed to be a numeric literal with optional unary minus; this allows malformed input like `IDENTITY(- 2147483648, 1)`. Consider a dedicated SignedLiteralGrammar or merging sign into the literal.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepting NumericLiteralSegment is not documented or tested.
issues.detail: The grammar now allows a numeric literal for DEFAULT_LANGUAGE (e.g., language ID), but the PR description only mentions unquoted identifier support, and no fixture exercises the numeric form. Either add a test case or remove the unused alternative to keep the grammar minimal.

issues.description: DROP CONSTRAINT now treats CONSTRAINT keyword as optional inside the delimited list, which is semantically wrong.
issues.detail: The inner Sequence wraps `CONSTRAINT` plus IfExistsGrammar with optional=True, so `ALTER TABLE t DROP <objref>, <objref>` parses without ever stating CONSTRAINT. Valid T-SQL requires CONSTRAINT (or COLUMN) to disambiguate. Tighten the grammar so the keyword is required at least once per clause.

issues.description: New declare_table_type fixture lacks a trailing semicolon/GO, inconsistent with the file's style.
issues.detail: All other DECLARE @table examples in declare_table_type.sql end with `;`. The added `declare @var table (...)` block omits the terminator. Not a parse error but inconsistent and could mask whether the parser actually emits a statement_terminator node here.

review.summary: The diff adds useful TSQL parsing coverage (table-var indexes, CREATE LOGIN options, signed identity seeds, multi-DROP ALTER TABLE), but the ALTER TABLE refactor removes the outer Delimited wrapper, which regresses multi-clause ALTER TABLE statements that were previously supported (and explicitly removed from fixtures). The signed identity seed grammar and DROP CONSTRAINT keyword optionality also have subtle correctness gaps worth tightening before merge. Other items are minor consistency/documentation nits.
